title: Bag Charge by Place in the Count — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand
content:
**Airport services charging clause — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** The charge for a checked bag of the ticket's first unflown segment is set as follows.

1. **Direction.** The bag's direction is the return on a partially flown round trip and the outbound otherwise.
2. **Free allowance.** The free allowance is the most generous of the fare brand's checked-bag allowance for the ticket's itinerary class, the elite checked-bag allowance of an active Summit membership the ticket credits, and, on a ticket naming an active corporate agreement, the agreement tier's corporate checked-bag allowance; the allowances never add together.
3. **Place in the count.** The bag's place in the count is the number of first, second and third bag charges already recorded in the bag's direction plus one.
4. **Check-in channel.** The segment's check-in channel is the airport when any bag charge of that segment was paid at the airport, online when a bag charge of that segment was paid online and none at the airport, and the call center otherwise.
5. **List charge.** The bag's list charge is zero when its place in the count is within the free allowance; beyond it, a first bag on a domestic itinerary costs the fare brand's online first-bag fee when the segment's check-in channel is online and its airport first-bag fee otherwise, a second domestic bag costs the second-bag fee, a first or second bag on an international itinerary costs the first-bag or second-bag fee of its itinerary class, and a third or later bag costs the third-bag fee of domestic and short-haul itineraries or of long-haul itineraries.
6. **Charge posted.** The bag charge posted is the bag's list charge rounded to the cent.

The first unflown segment is the segment whose number is one more than the number of coupons already flown. The fees and brand allowances are those of the ticket's fare brand in its bag tariff.

## Allowance table (hypothetical allowances)

| Fare brand allowance | Elite allowance (active membership) | Corporate allowance (active agreement) | Free allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | None | 1 |
| 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 |
| 2 | Membership not active | None | 2 |

## Worked example (hypothetical fees)

A round-trip domestic ticket has its outbound flown, so a bag now checked travels on the return. The free allowance is 1. One first-bag charge is already recorded on the return, so the new bag's place in the count is 2. Suppose the fare brand's domestic second-bag fee were 50 dollars: the charge posted is 50.00 dollars. On the outbound, with no bag charge yet recorded, a bag would take place 1 and fall within the allowance, charged at 0.00.
